paper_sections.title: Ventromedial Prefrontal Cortex Encodes Emotional Value
Effects of emotion experience and regulation
Neural response to normative valence by condition
pvmPFC activation is associated with differences in behavioral ratings

description.value: The study investigated how cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative emotional images affects valuation-related activity in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex, using subjective and normative valence ratings.

design.value: Two independent experimental samples of human participants performed a cognitive reappraisal task while undergoing fMRI. Exp1 was newly collected and Exp2 was a replication sample drawn from a previously published study.

description.value: After each trial, participants rated how positive or negative they felt after having implemented the strategy.
Exp2 participants scored at 27 or higher.

source_definition.value: Positive, negative, or neutral emotional valence of the images, including participants' trial-by-trial ratings and normative IAPS ratings.
Experience versus Regulate cognitive reappraisal condition.
Mean-centered normative valence ratings for the IAPS stimuli.
Trial-by-trial estimates of pvmPFC activation extracted from an independently defined posterior vmPFC ROI.

description.value: 31 younger adults between the ages of 19 and 40 years (mean 25; 10 males). Participants reported no history of psychiatric or neurological problems or contraindications to fMRI scanning.

exclusion_criteria.value: history of psychiatric or neurological problems

medical_condition.value: no history of psychiatric or neurological problems

description.value: 22 younger adults between the ages of 19 and 33 years (mean 23; 11 males).
20 older adults between the ages of 59 and 73 years (mean 69; 10 males).

inclusion_criteria.value: scored at 27 or higher on the Folstein Mini-Mental State Examination

description.value: Exp2 comprised 20 older adults and 22 younger adults.

task_description.value: Participants viewed images from the International Affective Picture System and were asked either to regulate their emotions using cognitive reappraisal or to experience their emotions naturally.

instructions.value: For the Experience condition, participants were instructed to experience their emotions naturally. For the Regulate condition, participants were asked to emotionally detach themselves from the image.

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System, categorized as positive, negative, or neutral based on normative IAPS ratings.

task_description.value: Replication sample performing a nearly identical cognitive reappraisal task while undergoing fMRI.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to either experience their emotions naturally or use cognitive reappraisal to emotionally detach themselves from the image; Exp2 used the cue “Decrease”.

stimuli.value: Images from the International Affective Picture System.

description.value: Functional data were acquired using a gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence with 30 axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane, FOV = 256 mm, and flip angle = 60°.
Functional data were acquired with 34 slices, flip angle = 90°, and voxel size = 3.75 × 3.75 × 3.8 mm.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration of the functional data; whole brain coverage with 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.
A high-resolution inversion-recovery prepared SPGR anatomical image was used for normalization and coregistration; whole brain coverage with 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxels.
fMRI preprocessing included motion correction, brain extraction, spatial smoothing, high-pass filtering, and normalization to standard space.

steps.value: spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 6 mm (FWHM)
normalization using transforms estimated from each participant's own high-resolution anatomical image and FSL's MNI template using FLIRT
runs with >5 volumes with movement of >1 mm in any direction were discarded

model_settings.value: One regressor of interest was created for each trial type; nuisance regressors modeled initial picture presentation and response period. First-level models corrected for local autocorrelation.
Combined the data across all runs within a single participant.
Valence and condition were modeled as fixed effects and each participant as a random effect; restricted maximum likelihood estimation and a variance components covariance structure were used.

The amplitude of the event-related response was modulated by participants' ratings for each image. The parametric regressor was orthogonalized to the main effect and a quadratic regressor was included to control for nonlinear results.

definition.value: The amplitude of the event-related response was modulated by participants' ratings for each image; increasingly positive valence ratings were associated with increased activation in the Experience condition

name.value: Neural response to normative valence by condition

roi_definition.value: a region of interest in the posterior vmPFC (pvmPFC) was defined based on coordinates drawn from a previous study

definition.value: IAPS normative rating by condition interaction on pvmPFC activation; the effect of IAPS rating was significant in the experience condition, but not in the regulation condition

name.value: pvmPFC activation is associated with differences in behavioral ratings

definition.value: A GLM including experiment number, IAPS normative ratings, condition, the interaction of IAPS normative ratings and condition, and trial-by-trial estimates of pvmPFC activation predicted trial-by-trial valence ratings

name.value: Behavioral effects of emotion experience and regulation

definition.value: Valence and condition were modeled as fixed effects and each participant as a random effect
Valenced stimuli (Positive vs Negative) that had been regulated and neutral images that had been experienced

title.value: Effect of reappraisal, IAPS rating, and pvmPFC activation on behavior

caption.value: Effect of reappraisal, IAPS rating, and pvmPFC activation on behavior

footer.value: GLM revealed that IAPS normative rating, condition, and an IAPS normative-rating-by-condition interaction predicted valence ratings. In addition, there was also a significant relationship between pvmPFC activation and behavior. *Significant.

description.value: Regression coefficients for experiment, IAPS normative rating, condition, the IAPS normative-rating-by-condition interaction, and pvmPFC activation predicting behavioral valence ratings.
